import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    readings = inputs["readings"].copy()
    
    # Step 1: Mark rows as bad based on row rule
    # value IS NULL OR value < 0 OR value > 1000 -> BAD
    readings["is_bad"] = (
        readings["value"].isna() | 
        (readings["value"] < 0) | 
        (readings["value"] > 1000)
    )
    
    # Step 2: Group by batch_id and evaluate batch rule
    batch_stats = readings.groupby("batch_id").agg(
        total_rows=("reading_id", "count"),
        bad_row_count=("is_bad", "sum")
    ).reset_index()
    
    # Calculate batch reject percentage (for quarantined batches)
    batch_stats["batch_reject_pct"] = (
        batch_stats["bad_row_count"] * 100.0 / batch_stats["total_rows"]
    ).round(2)
    
    # Determine which batches to quarantine: bad_row_count * 100 > total_rows * 20
    batch_stats["quarantine"] = (
        batch_stats["bad_row_count"] * 100 > batch_stats["total_rows"] * 20
    )
    
    # Step 3: Merge batch decisions back to readings
    readings = readings.merge(batch_stats[["batch_id", "quarantine", "batch_reject_pct"]], 
                               on="batch_id", how="left")
    
    # Step 4: Route rows to appropriate output tables
    readings_clean = pd.DataFrame(columns=["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value"])
    readings_rejects = pd.DataFrame(columns=["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value"])
    readings_quarantine = pd.DataFrame(columns=["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value", "batch_reject_pct"])
    
    # Separate quarantined batches
    quarantined_mask = readings["quarantine"] == True
    if quarantined_mask.any():
        quarantine_data = readings[quarantined_mask][["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value", "batch_reject_pct"]]
        readings_quarantine = quarantine_data
    
    # For non-quarantined batches, separate good and bad rows
    non_quarantined = readings[quarantined_mask == False]
    if len(non_quarantined) > 0:
        good_rows = non_quarantined[non_quarantined["is_bad"] == False][["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value"]]
        bad_rows = non_quarantined[non_quarantined["is_bad"] == True][["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value"]]
        
        if len(good_rows) > 0:
            readings_clean = good_rows
        if len(bad_rows) > 0:
            readings_rejects = bad_rows
    
    # Reset index and ensure proper dtypes
    readings_clean = readings_clean.reset_index(drop=True)
    readings_rejects = readings_rejects.reset_index(drop=True)
    readings_quarantine = readings_quarantine.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Ensure columns are in correct order and dtypes
    readings_clean = readings_clean[["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value"]]
    readings_rejects = readings_rejects[["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value"]]
    readings_quarantine = readings_quarantine[["batch_id", "reading_id", "sensor", "value", "batch_reject_pct"]]
    
    return {
        "readings_clean": readings_clean,
        "readings_rejects": readings_rejects,
        "readings_quarantine": readings_quarantine
    }
